ambiguity: A 'Network error' toast from Gitea's own UI when clicking 'Create squash commit' reads as a Gitea frontend/merge bug (D) or a browser/client network problem (A); C only if one infers that the request never reached Gitea. Body mentions Docker on EC2, no proxy/WAF; the decisive 403 page is only visible in the screenshot, which the triager cannot see.
decisive_code: web_src/js/features/common-global.js:fetchActionDoRequest (used by the form-fetch-action merge form in web_src/js/components/PullRequestMergeForm.vue): 'Network error' (i18n.network_error) is shown only in the catch branch, i.e. when fetch fails or a 4xx body is not JSON; routers/web/repo/pull.go:MergePullRequest answers every 4xx outcome with ctx.JSONError/JSONRedirect (valid JSON) and uses ctx.ServerError (logged, toast 'server error: 500') otherwise; the router logger (modules/web/routing/logger.go) logs every request. 'Network error' + no server log line for the request => a non-Gitea component answered with a non-JSON error page (WAF 403).
notes: A WAF rule in front of Gitea blocked the merge POST; no code change.

reviews.decidable_why: 'No logs present in the Gitea server' and the 403 proxy page in the screenshot point to something in front of Gitea, but the WAF is not named.
The body only says 'Network error' with no server logs. The WAF/proxy is never mentioned, and the screenshot alone hints at a proxy 403.
